Moreover, lexical information needs to be supported by the appropriate prosodic component to enable people to correctly perceive secondary emotions [8], i.e., the sentence for which emotional speech is synthesised has to be correctly modelled at the accent and phrase levels in alignment with what is being said. Modelling the secondary emotions by handcrafted feature extraction on a relatively small database, as described in this paper, leads to developing a low-resource emotional speech synthesis system. In this paper, the focus was on developing a low-resource approach for emotional speech synthesis of five secondary emotions by modelling prosody features. Contour-level modelling of  was used for emotional speech synthesis in a study [15] based on the ToBI model (a qualitative model).
